newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD-led states see risk of German budget overshoot.
newsitem.headline: SPD-led states see risk of German budget overshoot.

text.p: Federal states controlled by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Wednesday that Germany risked running excessive budget deficits both this year and next, and government finances may not be sustainable.

"For both 1997 and 1998 we fear there will be excessive current deficits and a further increase in the national debt," the states said in a joint statement after a meeting of the finance planning council.

The SPD rules alone or in coalition in a majority of German federal states, which together with local governments and a Bundesbank representive took part in the occasional finance planning council meeting with Finance Minister Theo Waigel.

The SPD group also warned Germany might be able to achieve only a "one-off", but not a lasting, fulfilment of the Maastricht treaty criteria governing which countries can join European economic and monetary union (EMU)

"Even if we manage to meet the criteria to join the third stage of EMU through one-off measures in 1997, the reference year, it is not certain now whether Germany will achieve sustainably stable finances," the statement continued.

Tight spending control, a cut in non-wage labour costs and fundamental income tax reforms were vital to restore state finances, the group said. But, it added, there was no room for the big tax cuts Waigel is planning over the next two years.

No agreement was reached on creating an internal 'stability pact' to match the deal to enforce budget discipline under EMU at national level pushed through by Germany at the recent European Union summit in Amsterdam. But a deal is likely soon.
"The federal and state governments want during the course of 1997 to agree on an internal process," the statement said.
